To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the levels of cyclic AMP binding proteins were higher in human breast tumours than in normal breast tissue, and that the levels of binding proteins correlated with the levels of the oestrogen receptor and the progesterone receptor.

the levels of cyclic AMP binding proteins were significantly higher in tumours than in matched adjacent non-tumorous tissues and that the levels of binding proteins correlated with tumour grade, tumour size, oestrogen receptor status, and progesterone receptor status.

the levels of cyclic AMP binding proteins were higher in breast cancer cytosols than in those of normal breast tissue, and were correlated with tumour size, histological grade and oestrogen receptor levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the measurement of cyclic AMP binding proteins and the application of such an assay to human breast cancer.
the measurement of cyclic AMP binding proteins and the relationship with other parameters in human breast cancer.
the development of methods which can be applied to the analysis of the biochemical and biological properties of breast cancer and the relationships between these parameters and clinical features.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the levels of binding proteins in human mammary tumours are variable and that the variations in levels of binding may be related to variations in cellularity.

the binding protein is not a marker for breast cancer, but that it is a marker for a particular type of breast tumour, and that its measurement in tumour extracts may be of value in the assessment of the response to hormonal manipulation.
the binding proteins are present in all breast tumours, but their levels vary considerably between individual tumours and between portions of the same individual tumour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the levels of cyclic AMP binding proteins are not correlated with tumour size, histological grade, oestrogen receptor status, progesterone receptor status, or with the presence or absence of lymph node metastases.
the levels of binding proteins in human tumours are variable but that the assay is reproducible and that it can detect the binding of cyclic AMP to the proteins in tumour cytosol.

the levels of cyclic AMP binding proteins are not correlated with tumour size, histological grading, oestrogen receptor status, progesterone receptor status, or with the clinical stage of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method is suitable for measuring cyclic AMP (cAMP) binding proteins in human tumours and that the binding proteins are widely present in human breast cancer cytosols.
there is no single factor which is responsible for the variations in levels of binding protein between tumours.
the binding proteins are not a homogeneous population and that they can vary considerably between tumours and even within a single tumour.
